Audit fundamentals
Planning the audit
The auditor plans the engagement before fieldwork begins, and records the plan in the audit file.
Evidence must be sufficient and appropriate for the opinion given.[1] It is gathered throughout the engagement.
[Note 1] As defined in the synthetic auditing standard used for these tests, which requires:
[Note 1] • a written plan
[Note 1]   • approved by the engagement partner
[Note 1] • a record of the evidence
[Note 1] Other standards may differ.
The sample size is forty items for each branch.
1. Agree the scope with management
  1. Confirm the branches in scope
  2. Confirm the reporting period
2. Collect the evidence
The procedures below are performed in order.
1. Inspect the records
2. Reperform the key controls
The reperformance described in item b) above is required for every branch.
Recording results
Kiểm toán viên phải ghi chép đầy đủ bằng chứng kiểm toán.
[Table 1, row 1] Column 1: Audit scope; Column 2: All branches
[Table 1, row 2] Column 1: Period; Column 2: FY2026 [2] [Note 2] The period runs from 1 July to 30 June. • Interim work in March
[Table 2, row 1] Risk: Missing records; Likelihood: Medium; Impact: Controls: • Monthly check • Manager sign-off
[Table 2, row 2] Risk: Missing records; Likelihood: Low; Impact: Low
[Table 2, row 3] Risk: Rủi ro gian lận; Likelihood: High; Impact: Owners: [Table 2.1 row 1: Control: Review, Owner: Finance manager]
Results are reported to the audit committee within ten business days of the end of fieldwork.[3]
[Note 3] The committee's timetable is set out below.
[Note 3] 1. Draft report
[Note 3] 2. Final report
